question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom

Get down to brass tacks
solution:
The correct answer is** Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Get down to brass tacks"** means to start discussing **the most important or fundamental aspects of a situation or problem**. (गंभीर होना)

 
 
• **Example: **Let's stop beating around the bush and **get down to brass tacks **about our financial issues.
 
 

Therefore, the correct meaning of the given idiom is** "To become serious about something".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Compromise, cooperation between people **(समझौता, लोगों के बीच सहयोग): A situation where conflicting parties make concessions to reach a mutually acceptable solution.

 
 
• **Example:** The two companies reached a **compromise **to avoid a lengthy legal battle.
 
 
 
• **Get fired from the job **(नौकरी से निकाल दिया जाना): To be dismissed from employment.
 
 
• **Example:** He was devastated after he** got fired from his job** due to budget cuts.
 
 
 
• **To be ready **(तैयार होना): To be prepared or set to begin.
 
 
• **Example:** She made sure everything was in place **to be ready **for the big presentation.
